items: **Dmitri and Debra are already 1st-degree LinkedIn connections** — he can write to her directly.
Valos already covers **device studies** as well as drug trials — a direct match for a first-in-human/feasibility device program.
Valos's European base (Genoa, Italy) is an advantage for a study run in **Spain**: same regulatory region (EU MDR) and time zone.

lead_with.title: Deliver what was promised, together
lead_with.text: Send the hourly rates, the Spanish partner shortlist and the preliminary study concept as **one package** — it shows control and speed.

lead_with.title: Design for feasibility, not just analysis
lead_with.text: Earlier stroke-cooling trials (EuroHYP-1, ICTuS 2/3) stopped early because cooling targets and recruitment were not feasible. Show how Valos's design would measure exactly that: time to target temperature, protocol adherence, recruitment rate.

lead_with.title: Use the latest evidence
lead_with.text: The CHILL-ART trial (ESOC, May 2026) reported better 90-day functional independence with intra-arterial cooling during thrombectomy — a useful anchor for endpoints and sample-size assumptions.

person.name: Debra Mitchell, PhD
person.text: Founder & President of **Beofor Research Consulting** (since May 2025, Toronto): clinical research and medical affairs strategy for biotechs, including **CRO oversight** and vendor optimization. Before that, **16 years at Janssen (J&J)**, latest as Director, Global Clinical Program Leader; also ex-Eli Lilly. Her headline cites 150+ studies, 50+ countries and a $1B+ portfolio. She is already **connected to Dmitri on LinkedIn**. She chooses vendors for a living — expect a rigorous qualification.

company.text: Hybernia Medical develops an endovascular catheter system that cools the brain locally (selective hypothermia) during stroke procedures, to protect tissue and limit reperfusion injury. It started as a Columbia University spin-off, is based in Uniondale, New York, and holds US patents on estimating regional metabolic rate and blood flow from heat. Its founders co-edited a Frontiers in Neurology series on brain hypothermia and neuroprotection.

financials.text: Small private company (1–50 people). A third-party directory lists about **$3.7M raised** with support from the NIH, New York State and the Dana Foundation — _unverified, treat as indicative_. Budget sensitivity is likely: lead with hourly rates and a phased scope.

history.text: Meeting held with Audrey, Francesco, Sergey and Andrea about the follow-up feasibility study in Spain. Agreed: Valos sends senior statistical study-design hourly rates, identifies Spanish regulatory and operational partners, and drafts a preliminary study concept. Hybernia sends a vendor qualification questionnaire. Broader scope and pricing come once the design is clear. Background: Hybernia's 8-patient Post-MECC feasibility study ran at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital (Barcelona) from June to October 2025.

industry.title: Intra-arterial cooling is back
industry.text: At ESOC 2026, CHILL-ART (26 centers, 262 patients) reported more than half of cooled patients functionally independent at 90 days vs 39.8% with sham; another Chinese phase 3 trial showed conflicting results.

industry.title: Feasibility is the known failure point
industry.text: Systemic cooling trials EuroHYP-1 (98 of 1,500 patients) and ICTuS 2/3 (120 of 1,600) stopped early for slow recruitment or poor target attainment — the reason a well-designed feasibility study matters.

talking_points: What is the primary objective in Spain — device performance, safety, or feasibility for a pivotal trial?
How many sites and patients are you planning, and have Spanish sites already been approached?
Will the study run under EU MDR as a clinical investigation, and who is the EU legal representative?
Which endpoints matter most for your next financing or FDA discussion?
When can we expect the vendor qualification questionnaire?

posts.text: “Not every problem needs automation.” Before buying a tool, define the problem: is it process, people, data or technology?
posts.use: If AI comes up, frame Valos's AI work as fixing defined bottlenecks, not tech for its own sake.

posts.text: Programs struggle on execution, not science — they need clarity on decision rights, accountability, **vendor oversight**, resources and milestones.
posts.use: Show the governance Valos offers: named senior statistician, escalation path, milestone reporting.

posts.text: A biotech's Phase II was inspection-ready but not **evidence-ready**: endpoints, registry design and the CRO statement of work had ignored publication and payer needs.
posts.use: Propose that the Spain study concept is designed to be evidence-ready from day one (publications, next financing).

posts.text: Her rules: she doesn't work for free, every meeting needs a **clear purpose**, she declines cold outreach and checks LinkedIn twice a week.
posts.use: Send a tight agenda before any call and reach her by email.

posts.text: Regulators look for process awareness — “can you defend why a vendor was **qualified and selected**?”
posts.use: Have Valos's QA and vendor-qualification answers ready before her questionnaire arrives.

posts.text: A protocol amendment costs about **$500,000** and months of delay; the fix is robust design with KOLs and regulators up front.
posts.use: Position Valos's senior study design as amendment insurance.

hooks: Hybernia's first study, **Post-MECC (NCT06634303)**, was an 8-patient device feasibility study at **Vall d'Hebron, Barcelona**, completed in October 2025 — the new Spanish study builds on it.
Debra **co-developed statistical analysis plans, designed CRFs and revamped RfP processes** at J&J — she will judge Valos's study-design depth personally.
Her own words: “If you want better outcomes, ask better questions” — start by asking what the Spain study must prove for Hybernia's next step.
Like Ali Ashrafzadeh at Electra, she is **ex-Eli Lilly** (and 16 years at J&J/Janssen).
She values long-term partnerships (“with CROs and vendors, think of how you can work together for the long term”) — present Valos for the program, not one study.
